trajectory_summary: This is a pre-qualified, pre-warmed lead who did most of the selling-herself work before the rep said much of substance — she disclosed a cancelled competitor contract, a specific technical need (battery backup for a boiler), a positive prior impression of Ion, and a recurring autonomy/control concern. The rep executed the mechanical verification (address, credit, bill, scheduling) competently and booked a specific day/time, but never engaged with any of the substantive content the customer handed over, leaving real handoff risk for the closer. The call shape is mixed: forward motion on logistics, but flat-to-leaking on the relationship and technical-question front.

observed_outcome.quote: We could do 02:30 on Friday. Would that work?
observed_outcome.reasoning: Rep offers a specific day (Friday) and time (02:30), customer confirms understanding after clarifying AM/PM confusion, and the rep explicitly restates it ('So Friday at 02:30? Sounds good?') with the customer's agreement at 10:47 ('Sounds good.'). Rep also frames it as an 'in person appointment with my specialist' at 08:11, making this a locked, dated, timed booking.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep never asks for or receives a dollar bill amount — only kWh usage via a bill photo. Customer never states an average monthly bill dollar figure on the call, so there is no number to flip.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: Rep asks for the utility bill, sets up text-based photo delivery ('Send you over a text message... upload a photo of that bar graph'), and the customer successfully sends the screenshot which the rep confirms receiving at 08:09-08:11.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asks 'what interested you in solar' — the customer volunteers her reason unprompted at 00:14 (dissatisfaction with a competitor's contract terms). The rep acknowledges generically ('Alright. Sounds good. Yeah. We can do what we can do for you') but never ties the appointment or booking back to resolving that specific contract-terms concern.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Naming the recurring autonomy/control theme back to the customer
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I am not trying to be told what I can and cannot do on my property for the next twenty five years.
primary_coaching_focus.why: This customer raised the same underlying concern four times in different forms (contract restrictions at 01:44, contract clause detail at 05:21, autopay/account control at 07:33, AI-vetting intent at 10:25) and the rep never once reflected it back. A single acknowledgment early would have de-risked the entire appointment and given the closer a clean, named concern to open with instead of discovering it cold.

key_moments.quote: I am not trying to be told what I can and cannot do on my property for the next twenty five years.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the customer naming her single biggest deal-risk with the prior company — restrictive contract language. The rep never reflects this back or reassures her about Ion's terms. Strategic read: rep may be intentionally deferring all contract-specifics to the closer (consistent with scope discipline). Reactive read: a brief acknowledgment ('that's a fair concern, our specialist will walk through exactly what you can and can't do') costs nothing and reduces closer-stage risk.

key_moments.quote: I need a battery backup system for just my boiler.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a specific, concrete need (small battery backup, not a full Powerwall) — a hook the rep could reflect back as something Ion's specialist can size specifically for her. Rep instead moves to generic estimate language.

Customer just explained she'd freeze in winter without power for her boiler and can't afford a $10,000 battery. This is a genuine practical/financial vulnerability disclosure, and the rep's response is a flat filler line with no acknowledgment of the freezing-in-winter stakes she raised.

Customer is describing exactly which clause in the competitor's contract her AI flagged (no outside power sources including generators) — this is competitive intelligence a closer would want. The rep's response is a passive filler, not a probing follow-up.
